title: Bible Verses for Strength, and How to Pray Them | Prayed
headline: Bible verses for strength, for when you have run out of your own
dek: Seventeen verses for the end of your reserves, for the long carry, and for where the strength is actually coming from. With a short prayer to write for each.
desc: Seventeen Bible verses for strength from the World English Bible, grouped for the days there is nothing left, the stretches you have to keep going anyway, and where the strength is actually coming from. With a short prayer to write for each group.
card: Seventeen verses for the end of your reserves, for the long carry, and for where the strength is actually coming from.
intro: Strength is the wrong word for what most people are after when they go looking for verses about it. Nobody types it into a search box wanting to be stronger in general. They want to get through Thursday, or through the next six months of caring for someone, or through a job they cannot leave yet. The request is nearly always specific, and it is usually made by someone already running on very little.

The verses below are quoted word for word from the World English Bible and grouped by where you are rather than by book. Read what they actually claim. Most of them do not say you will find reserves you did not know you had. They say the opposite: the strength belongs to someone else and is being lent, and the qualification for receiving it is having none of your own.

One plain thing first. Tiredness that does not lift after rest is not always a spiritual problem, and these verses are not a substitute for a doctor. Exhaustion is a symptom of a long list of ordinary treatable things, and of depression, and it is worth saying out loud to someone who can test for them. Read the group that matches this week and leave the rest.

paras: This is the end of the reserves. Not a hard day, which you can do, but the point after a run of them where the ordinary things have started costing what the hard things used to cost. You are still functioning, probably. You are just doing it on nothing.
Scripture is unusually blunt here. These verses do not tell you that you are stronger than you think. Three of them begin by agreeing that you have run out, and then say what happens after that.

verses.note: The failing is in the present tense and it is not walked back. The psalm concedes the whole first clause and puts something behind it, rather than arguing you out of it.
The qualification is having no might. Written to people who had been in exile long enough to stop expecting anything.

Paul had asked three times for the thing to be taken away, and this is the answer he got instead. Made perfect in weakness means the weakness is where the power works, not the obstacle it works around.
The answer came the same day, and what arrived was strength in his soul rather than a change to the situation he was calling about.
In trouble, not after it. The opening phrase is the psalm's own musical heading, carried in by the translation. A very present help is the part to sit on: the claim is about proximity.

sections.pray: I have nothing left and I am tired of pretending otherwise. My heart is failing. You say you give power to people with no might, so I am asking as one of those, today and not later, for enough to get through what is actually in front of me.

sections.h2: When you have to keep going anyway
paras: The harder case is not the day you collapse. It is the stretch where collapsing is not available. Someone depends on you, the treatment runs another eight months, the job has to be kept until something else comes up. You are not asking to be rescued from it. You are asking to carry it without breaking, which is a smaller prayer and a different one.
These verses are about the long carry, and they are worth reading for their pace. Almost none of them promise speed, and one offers rest and then hands you something to carry.

verses.note: He says rest and then immediately says yoke, which reads oddly. A yoke is not a way of stopping. It is a way of pulling a load that spreads the weight: the offer is to be put in one with him, not let out of the field.
Mount up, run, walk. The list gets less impressive as it goes, and the last item is the one most people need. Renew assumes waiting first, which is the part nobody wants.
Paul grants the decay of the outward person without softening it. Day by day is a rate rather than a total, which is the honest scale for a long stretch.

The most quoted verse about strength and the most often bent. Two verses earlier Paul says what all things means: he has learned to be content hungry or full. It is about enduring circumstances, not achieving what you have decided to achieve.
The command is to be strong, and both halves of the sentence then place the strength outside you. It opens the passage about armour, all of which is worn rather than generated.

sections.pray: I am not asking to be let out of this. I am asking to be able to carry it. Renew what I have day by day, at whatever rate you do that, and let walking without fainting count as an answer, because it would be one.

sections.h2: Where the strength is actually coming from
paras: The verses in this last group are the ones people skip, because they look like praise rather than help. Between them they name where the strength is kept, and the answer is never inside the person praying.

Two of them are songs, and one was written down as a song deliberately, by a man who had just been told the invasion was coming and would not be called off. That is the shape of most of these: not relief, but something to stand on while the thing you feared happens anyway.

verses.note: Seven images in one sentence: rock, fortress, deliverer, refuge, shield, horn, high tower. Every one is something you stand on or shelter behind. None of them is something you turn into.

Habakkuk wrote this at the end of a book about an invasion God had confirmed was coming. Deer's feet are for staying upright on ground that is steep and loose. The last line is his instruction to the musicians.

The crowd was weeping as the law was read to them, and this is the response: eat, drink, and send a portion to someone who has nothing prepared. The joy is described as the source rather than the result.
Watch the order. Trusted, then helped, then the heart rejoices, then the song. The gladness is downstream of being helped and is not asked for first.
Sung on the far side of the water, looking back at it. Strength and song arrive in the same breath, which is the pattern across this whole group.

Isaiah is quoting the song from Exodus, centuries later, to a different people facing a different threat. That is what these last two verses recommend: when your own words run out, sing an old one about a rescue you did not see.

sections.pray: I have been trying to be the strong one and it is not a thing I can be. You are the rock and I am not. Be my strength today in the plain sense of the word, and if a song is part of how that arrives, teach me one, because I do not have one at the moment.

closing_h2: Write down the weeks you got through, and date them
closing: Strength is almost impossible to assess from inside a hard stretch. The weeks you did get through leave no mark, so they stop counting, and the impression that you have been failing the whole time goes unchallenged because there is nothing to check it against. A dated record is the plain correction.

Prayed keeps that record for you. Write the prayer in your own words, and the app matches verses like the ones on this page to what you wrote, so you are not hunting for a reference at the end of a day that took everything. Each prayer comes back to you at three days, a week, a month and a year, which means the Tuesday you did not think you could do is handed back later with the date on it and whatever happened next. Nothing you write leaves your phone, and writing is free.

Start with this week, in one sentence, with the date. Write down the thing you are not sure you can keep doing. In a year you will either still be doing it or you will know why you stopped, and either way the record will tell you something your memory will not.
